 On the show Ethel Kennedy ‘Crawled Into Bed’ With Jackie Kennedy As She Was Dying of Cancer, Kerry Kennedy Recalls
 The daughter of Robert F. Kennedy remembered a touching moment between her mom and Jacqueline Kennedy Onassis before the former first lady died in 1994. Oct. 12, 2026, 11:06 AM EDT / Source : TODAY Scott Stump
 Kerry Kennedy Talks New Book Honoring Mother Ethel’s Legacy 07:57 Share Add TODAY to Google Kerry Kennedy is shining a light on the relationship between her mother, Ethel Kennedy, and former first lady Jacqueline Kennedy Onassis, with a tender remembrance of a moment the women shared before Onassis’ death from cancer in 1994. 
 Kerry Kennedy, 67, daughter of the late Ethel and Robert F. Kennedy, spoke with Craig Melvin on TODAY Oct. 12 about how she went with her mother to visit Onassis in her aunt’s final hours. 
 “On the last day, when she was dying, mom and I went over to see her,” Kerry Kennedy said. “And it was very special because mommy crawled into bed with her and talked about her faith and their lives together and all they had been through, and it was just a beautiful, spiritual moment.” 
 Kerry Kennedy details the relationship between her mother and the wife of late President John F. Kennedy in her new book, “Ethel Kennedy: The Extraordinary Life and Bold Legacy,” which will be released on Oct. 13. 
 “The two sisters-in-law had such different personalities: Jackie was understated and reserved; Mum was the opposite, outgoing and exuberant. But they had a special bond from their shared history, and they often sent each other sweet notes and gifts over the years,” Kerry Kennedy writes.
 Jackie Kennedy Onassis and Ethel Kennedy during RFK Pro Celebrity Tennis Tournament in August 1975. Ron Galella / Ron Galella Collection via Getty Ethel and Kerry Kennedy visited Onassis at her Manhattan apartment when she was receiving hospice care at the end of her life. Kerry Kennedy recalled how her mother and Onassis reminisced about times they shared when she was first dating John F. Kennedy. 
 “Then Mum whispered a few words to her, lay down next to her, and said the Rosary with her,” Kerry Kennedy writes. “It was a moment of tenderness, of holiness, of shared life and shared tragedy. A moment when everything melted away until only love remained.” 
 Kerry Kennedy also writes about how the two first met in 1953 when her mother threw a St. Patrick’s Day party, and “the two women hit it off right away.” 
 “They were nearly the same age, shared a deep Catholic faith, and were both mad about horses, interior design, and two Kennedy brothers,” she writes. 
 John F. Kennedy would often bring Onassis over to Robert and Ethel Kennedy’s home when the two were dating, according to Kerry Kennedy. She refers to Onassis as Aunt Jackie throughout the book. 
 “They bonded very early. My mother loved Jackie, and I think that was mutual,” she said on TODAY.
 Ethel Kennedy, who had 11 children with Robert F. Kennedy , died at 96 in 2024 , leaving behind a legacy that includes 34 grandchildren and 24 great grandchildren. She was married to the former U.S. attorney general and New York senator for 18 years before he was assassinated by a gunman in 1968 with Ethel Kennedy right by his side. 
 “She’s a woman who went through such hardship in her life,” Kerry Kennedy said on TODAY. “She was at my father’s side when a man came out and killed my dad and shot five other people. 
 “It was a miracle she survived, and she came out of that not unable to get out of bed the next morning, but full of gusto, taking care of these 11 children, building Kennedy Human Rights (Center) and serving the world,” she added. “And she really grew through service and through faith, and I think that’s something all of us need today.”
